evidence.role: Dependency retrieval is grounded in the verified 9702_t01_cm03_l06 handoff; no new P2 demand is claimed

hints: For each error, describe what several repeated readings would look like.
Match the response to the pattern: remove a shared cause, or reduce two-sided variation.

walkthrough.text: A systematic error moves repeated measurements consistently in the same direction rather than producing an unpredictable spread.
Its cause must be found and corrected, for example through a zero check or calibration.
A random error varies unpredictably from reading to reading and creates scatter.
Several independent readings and their mean allow changes in opposite directions to partly cancel.

ai_rubric.observable: States that a systematic error shifts repeated measurements consistently in the same direction
Gives a suitable response to systematic error, such as checking zero, calibrating or correcting the identified cause
States that a random error varies unpredictably between readings and produces scatter
Gives repeated readings and calculation of a mean as a suitable response to random variation

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground judging precision from a small spread and accuracy by comparison with a true value; the mass values are original

hints: Compare the four readings with one another first.
Then compare their cluster with 40.00 g.

walkthrough.text: The range is 40.36 g - 40.35 g = 0.01 g, so the repeats agree closely and are precise.
Their mean is 40.355 g, about 0.36 g above the true value of 40.00 g.
The readings are therefore precise but not accurate, so select B.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects precise but not accurate because the repeated readings have a small range but lie far above 40.00 g

evidence.role: The mapped leaf grounds resolution as the smallest instrument division or step; the force-meter context is original

hints: Resolution is one smallest change shown by the instrument.
Use the stated display step directly.

walkthrough.text: The display changes by 0.01 N between adjacent readings.
That smallest distinguished change is the instrument resolution.
Select B, 0.01 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects 0.01 N as the smallest change distinguished by the display

evidence.role: Mapped leaves require separation of accuracy, precision and fine instrument scale; the general statement is newly authored

hints: Ask which property is actually described by a small scale step.
A zero error and reading scatter can still exist.

walkthrough.text: Fine resolution means the instrument can distinguish small changes.
It does not show whether repeated values agree or whether the result is close to truth.
Precision and accuracy must therefore be judged separately, so select C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects that fine resolution distinguishes small changes but does not by itself establish precision or accuracy

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground comparison of spread and closeness to a true value; the strip context, readings and number-line brief are original

hints: Use maximum minus minimum for each range.
Use the means to judge closeness to 8.00 cm and the ranges to judge agreement among repeats.

walkthrough.text: Calculate the two ranges from each maximum and minimum.
Add each set of four readings and divide by four to obtain the two means.
Use the smaller range to identify the more precise set and the mean closer to 8.00 cm to identify the more accurate set.

evidence.role: Grounds spread or range as the evidence for precision

hints: For each student, locate the largest and smallest reading.
Subtract the smallest from the largest and retain centimetres.

walkthrough.text: For P, range = 8.13 cm - 8.12 cm = 0.01 cm.
For Q, range = 8.06 cm - 7.94 cm = 0.12 cm.
Check that each range is non-negative and matches the full visual span of its data set.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the range of P as 0.01 cm
Calculates the range of Q as 0.12 cm

evidence.role: Grounds using a representative repeated result in comparison with a true value

hints: Add the four values in each row before dividing by four.
A mean must lie between the smallest and largest reading in its set.

walkthrough.text: P totals 32.50 cm, so its mean is 32.50 cm / 4 = 8.125 cm, or 8.13 cm at the reading scale.
Q totals 32.00 cm, so its mean is 32.00 cm / 4 = 8.00 cm.
Both means lie within their respective data ranges, providing an independent arithmetic check.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the mean of P as 8.125 cm, or 8.13 cm when rounded to the reading scale
Calculates the mean of Q as 8.00 cm

evidence.role: Directly grounds distinguishing agreement among repeats from closeness to truth

hints: Use the ranges for precision, not the distances from 8.00 cm.
Use the means for accuracy, not the widths of the sets.

walkthrough.text: P has the smaller range, 0.01 cm compared with 0.12 cm, so P is more precise.
Q has mean 8.00 cm, equal to the true length, while P's mean is about 0.13 cm high.
Q is therefore more accurate even though its readings are less precise.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies P as more precise because its range of 0.01 cm is smaller than Q's range of 0.12 cm
Identifies Q as more accurate because its mean of 8.00 cm equals the true length

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground instrument choice and the role of fine resolution; the supplied instrument card and object dimensions are original

hints: An instrument must physically include the object within its range.
It must also distinguish a step no larger than the change required.

walkthrough.text: Read the smallest distinguished step directly from each supplied resolution.
For each object, reject any instrument whose maximum range is too small.
Among instruments with enough range, choose one whose resolution meets the required step.
Keep zero error separate: fine resolution does not prevent a shared systematic offset.

evidence.role: Grounds resolution as the smallest distinguishable instrument step

hints: Read the calipers' resolution from the supplied instrument record.
State that value as a change in millimetres.

walkthrough.text: The record gives calipers resolution 0.1 mm.
Resolution is the smallest distinguished change, so the answer is 0.1 mm.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the calipers can distinguish a smallest change of 0.1 mm

evidence.role: Directly grounds selecting calipers for a roughly 12 cm object requiring a fine length reading

hints: First check whether 124 mm fits inside each maximum range.
Then compare the required 0.1 mm step with the supplied resolutions.

walkthrough.text: The micrometer's 25 mm range is too small for a 124 mm rod.
The metre rule has enough range but its 1 mm resolution is too coarse.
The calipers include 124 mm within their 150 mm range and distinguish 0.1 mm, so they meet both requirements.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects the calipers and states that their 150 mm range includes the 124 mm rod
States that the calipers' 0.1 mm resolution meets the required distinguishable step

evidence.role: Grounds choosing a micrometer when small diameter changes require finer resolution

hints: The wire diameter must fit within the instrument's range.
The instrument must separate changes of 0.01 mm.

walkthrough.text: A 0.60 mm diameter is well within the micrometer's 25 mm maximum range.
The required change is 0.01 mm, which equals the micrometer resolution.
The calipers and metre rule have coarser resolutions, so the micrometer is the suitable choice.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects the micrometer and states that its 25 mm range includes the 0.60 mm wire diameter
States that the micrometer's 0.01 mm resolution meets the required distinguishable change

evidence.role: Grounds separating a fine scale from accuracy relative to the true value

hints: State what a 0.01 mm resolution actually describes.
Accuracy requires a different comparison from the size of the scale step.

walkthrough.text: A 0.01 mm resolution means the micrometer can distinguish changes of 0.01 mm.
This says nothing by itself about the distance between a measured diameter and the true diameter.
Accuracy must be judged through closeness to truth, so fine resolution alone cannot establish it.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that fine resolution gives the smallest distinguishable change but does not show closeness to the true diameter

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground all three measurement-quality judgements; the prior Lesson 6 handoff supplies the signed zero-error correction. The balance record and values are original

hints: Treat mean, range, true value, empty reading and display step as evidence for different conclusions.
A correction that subtracts the same constant from every reading moves the set but does not change its width.

walkthrough.text: Calculate the mean and range before making any quality judgement.
Use the range for precision, the mean-to-true difference for accuracy and the display step for resolution.
Identify the positive empty reading as a systematic zero error and subtract it from the indicated mean.
Compare the corrected mean with truth and check whether subtracting a shared constant changed the range.

evidence.role: Grounds extracting a representative measured value and spread from repeated readings

hints: Add all five indicated values and divide by five.
Subtract the smallest reading from the largest for the range.

walkthrough.text: The five readings total 124.35 g, so mean = 124.35 g / 5 = 24.87 g.
The mean lies between the extreme readings, providing an independent check on the arithmetic.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the mean indicated reading as 24.87 g
Calculates the range of the indicated readings as 0.02 g

evidence.role: Directly grounds separate judgements of resolution, precision and accuracy

hints: Use the display step for resolution and the calculated range for precision.
For accuracy, compare 24.87 g with 24.39 g.

walkthrough.text: The smallest display change is 0.01 g, so this is the resolution.
The 0.02 g range is small, so the repeated readings are precise.
The mean differs from the true value by 24.87 g - 24.39 g = 0.48 g, so the uncorrected result is not accurate.

ai_rubric.observable: States the balance resolution as 0.01 g
Identifies the readings as precise because their range is only 0.02 g
Identifies the uncorrected readings as not accurate because their mean of 24.87 g is 0.48 g above the true value

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground the accuracy and precision consequences; the signed zero correction is grounded in the verified Lesson 6 handoff

hints: The empty instrument should read zero, so interpret the sign of its non-zero reading.
Subtracting the same amount from every reading shifts the centre but does not change the range.

walkthrough.text: The +0.48 g empty reading is a positive zero error and therefore a systematic error because it raises every indicated value by the same amount.
Corrected mean = 24.87 g - (+0.48 g) = 24.39 g.
The corrected mean now equals the true value, so accuracy is restored for this reference mass.
Subtracting 0.48 g from both the largest and smallest readings leaves their difference at 0.02 g, so precision is unchanged.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the +0.48 g empty reading as a positive systematic zero error because it shifts every reading upward
Subtracts 0.48 g from 24.87 g to obtain the corrected mean of 24.39 g
Explains that the correction restores accuracy to the true value but leaves precision unchanged because the 0.02 g range is unchanged

quality_audit.originality: All learner contexts, readings, instrument specifications and planned figures are original. No official wording, numerical data or diagram layout is reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The lesson teaches only precision, accuracy, instrument resolution, instrument selection and their connection to previously taught systematic, zero and random errors.
quality_audit.evidence: All eight mapped P2 leaves and all eight complete source-question contexts were reviewed. They ground the controlled meanings, comparison of repeated sets, low and high precision, accuracy relative to a true value, fine instrument divisions and suitable instrument selection. P1 evidence is deferred and was not inferred.
later_knowledge_excluded: uncertainty propagation through powers, products or quotients
later-topic physical principles from mixed source-question contexts
